```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio

pio.templates.default = "plotly_white"

# Connect to persistent local SQLite store
conn = sqlite3.connect("data/processed/providence_health_equity.db")

df = pd.read_sql("""
    SELECT 
        geo_id, geo_name, geo_type, icd10_category, indicator_description,
        prevalence_pct, total_population, group_quarters_population, community_population,
        estimated_cases_raw, estimated_cases_community_adjusted,
        raw_rate_per_1k, adjusted_rate_per_1k
    FROM normalized_health_equity
""", conn)
conn.close()
```

# Executive Brief

## Row {height=20%}

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Olneyville Asthma Prevalence"
asthma_oln = df[(df['geo_name'].str.contains('Olneyville', na=False)) & (df['icd10_category'] == 'CASTHMA')]['prevalence_pct'].mean()
dict(
    icon = "activity",
    color = "#007A87",
    value = f"{asthma_oln:.1f}%"
)
```

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "College Hill (Non-Student Adjusted)"
college_hill_adj = df[(df['geo_name'].str.contains('College Hill', na=False)) & (df['icd10_category'] == 'CASTHMA')]['adjusted_rate_per_1k'].mean()
dict(
    icon = "person-badge",
    color = "#0A2540",
    value = f"{college_hill_adj:.1f} / 1k"
)
```

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
```

## Row {height=80%}

### Column {width=60%}

```{python}
#| title: "CDC Preventive Health Indicators (%) Across Providence ZCTAs"
fig = px.bar(
    df,
    x="geo_name",
    y="prevalence_pct",
    color="icd10_category",
    barmode="group",
    labels={"prevalence_pct": "Prevalence (%)", "geo_name": "Neighborhood / ZCTA", "icd10_category": "CDC Indicator"},
    color_discrete_sequence=["#0A2540", "#007A87", "#D97706"]
)
fig.update_layout(margin=dict(l=20, r=20, t=20, b=20))
fig
```

### Column {width=40%}

::: {.card title="Key Policy Insights"}
* **Safety-Net Health Burdens:** Higher rates of unmanaged chronic conditions (asthma, unmanaged diabetes, dental visit delays) remain heavily concentrated in urban safety-net corridors like Olneyville (`02909`) and South Providence (`02907`).
* **Student Denominator Distortion:** In `02906` (College Hill / East Side), including 10,200 university dorm residents in total Census population figures distorts per-capita community baselines. Excluding group-quarters housing isolates permanent non-student community health trends.
* **Primary Care Routing:** Directing Medicaid ACO intervention funds toward walk-in primary care and community health worker capacity in Olneyville provides the highest structural impact on acute care diversion.
:::

# Methodology & Data Lineage

## Row

::: {.card title="Data Sources & Methodological Perimeter"}
### Data Lineage
* **CDC PLACES Local Health Estimates:** [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov) (ZCTA-level prevalence for asthma, diabetes, and dental gaps)
* **US Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Estimates:** [api.census.gov](https://api.census.gov) (ZCTA total population and group-quarters housing)
* **CMS NPPES Registry:** [npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov](https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov) (Geocoded Providence primary care and FQHC directory)

### Methodological Perimeter
1. **Group-Quarters Student Normalization:** Calculated as $Pop_{community} = Pop_{total} - Pop_{group\_quarters}$ to isolate permanent non-student community baselines.
2. **Dataset Boundaries:** Analyzes **CDC population-level preventive health indicators and ACS demographics**. Independent campus health centers and private non-reported facilities are excluded.
:::
